openings.claim: A broad resilient hand-held tapping face may spread force while repeated impulses lower the tile through bed movement.
openings.discriminator: Predicts fewer chips than a narrow face; relative adjustment time unspecified. Any chip or persistent height mismatch defeats adequacy.
openings.probe: Proposed comparison of chips and height change on sacrificial matched beds.
openings.uncertainty: Pad stiffness and curing sensitivity unknown; unspecified tile/bed properties prevent safety assurance.

openings.claim: Warming before tapping might change adhesive response and reduce the impulse needed for movement.
openings.discriminator: Easier adjustment than broad-pad tapping requires reversible warmth response; unchanged required impulse defeats advantage.
openings.probe: Only after explicit relaxation of no heating: compare warmed and ambient sacrificial beds.
openings.uncertainty: Currently incompatible with no heating; no thermal source supplied. Adhesive response and bond integrity unknown.

lineage.reason: Preserves distributed-contact impulse mechanism and chip/height discriminator.
Preserves a conditional thermal relation with its explicit constraint-relaxation gate.

Frame-mounted sustained distributed force predicts gradual movement but violates hand-held requirement. No impacts proves no safety; cracking, load and precision unresolved. Separate surrogate cracking study cannot establish in-case fit.

decision: All proposals and predictions are synthetic; no tile, adhesive or equipment is supplied. Require no edge chipping, hand-held adjustment and no adhesive heating. D1 is the current-fit hypothesis to probe, not an established solution. D2 needs explicit constraint relaxation; fixed press is excluded.
